# Command reference

<!-- GENERATED by docs/guide/tools/build_commands.js from Dashboard/commands.js - do not edit by hand, run the script again. -->

This chapter lists **every command** the dashboard can send: **181 commands** in 14 categories. 139 are swarm commands (`!`, 93 different first words), 34 are L2Swarm chat-box commands (`/`, 32 different first words) and 8 are dashboard actions. Safety: 25 safe, 135 confirm, 18 destructive.

The list is generated from the command catalog `Dashboard/commands.js`. That one file feeds both the command center on the page and the
server-side checks, so this reference always matches what the dashboard really sends. Words in the [glossary](06-glossary.md) are explained there.

## How to send a command

You have four ways. They all end up as the same chat line or action:

1. **Command center** (best): click the search field at the top of the dashboard (or press `Ctrl K` / `/` on a PC), type a few letters of
   the command, fill in the form, pick who gets it and press **Send**. You see exactly what is sent before you confirm. See
   [Command center](pages/command-center.md).
2. **Commands sheet**: the **Commands** button on a party card (Parties tab) or **All commands for &lt;name&gt;...** on a character page opens
   every command that fits that party or character, sorted by category.
3. **Quick buttons**: the party card has Status, Level, Supply, Collect, Class, Buff and Stop; the character page has Class change, Rebuff
   and Escape. They send the matching `!` command after one confirmation.
4. **By hand in L2Swarm**: type the swarm command in the chat box of the **party leader's** L2Swarm window with a `#` in front, for
   example `#!level`. `#` makes it a party chat line, which every window of the party reads. Do **not** type a bare `!level`: in the game
   a leading `!` means **shout**, and the line would go to everyone in the region. A character without a party gets the line as normal chat
   (the dashboard does that by itself). L2Swarm's own `/` commands are typed in that character's chat box as they are.

### The three kinds of command

| Starts with | Kind | Who receives it |
|---|---|---|
| `!` | **Swarm command**, handled by our script `swarm.js` | Party target: **once**, as party chat from the party leader; the whole party hears it. Character target: party chat from that character; only its own window obeys (a party leader's own line is heard by his whole party). All parties: once per party leader. Clan: every clan member. |
| `/` | **L2Swarm chat-box command** (built into L2Swarm) | Sent to **every chosen character one by one**. A party target means each member. |
| `@` | **Account action** (`@login`, `@logout`) | Opens or closes the account in L2Swarm for each chosen character. |

A few entries have no character at all (client mode switches and the PC buttons): the dashboard does those itself.

### Who acts

Many swarm commands are heard by the whole party, but only some of the characters act on them:

- `leader`: The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- `each`: **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- `self`: **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- `clanleader`: Only the **clan leader's** window acts; the target is always the clan leader.
- L2Swarm (`/`) commands and dashboard actions: each chosen character does it.

### Safety classes

- **safe** - only reports or a dry run; still asks once.
- **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that.

Every order shows a confirmation first (who gets it, how many characters, who is busy and will drop what they are doing). Passwords can
never be read or set from the dashboard, and `/config save` never takes a file name (saving to another file would re-point the account).

### Templates

The **Sends** line shows the exact text. `{name}` is replaced by what you fill in. A part in `[ ... ]` is left out when the argument inside
it is empty, for example `!sell[ {name}]` becomes `!sell` or `!sell Bryndis`.

### Free text

In the search field you can also type a plain phrase and choose **Tell them "..."**. The dashboard server turns it into a command when
you send it; the result line (and the message line under the header) shows what it became. It understands (case does not matter, "please", "now", "the", "team", "all" are ignored):

| You type | Becomes |
|---|---|
| restock, supply, supplies, buy supplies, shop scrolls | `!supply` |
| collect, collect adena | `!collect` |
| park, wait at grocer (optional: grocer, warehouse, weapons, start) | `!park grocer` (or the place you named) |
| class change, change class, profession | `!classchange` |
| forward drop on / forward drop off | `!cabinet Forward Drop on` / `off` |
| level, autolevel, grind, farm xp, lvl | `!level` |
| kill raid boss Bifrons, do raid boss Bifrons, raid Bifrons | `!mission raid Bifrons` |
| kill / attack &lt;monster&gt; | `!kill <monster>` |
| kamaloka 39, hall 33, labyrinth 56 (any two-digit level) | `!mission kamaloka 39` |
| kamaloka, dungeon, instance | `!mission kamaloka` |
| stop mission, abort mission | `!mission stop` |
| stop, halt, pause | `!stop` |
| status, report | `!status` |
| regroup, go home, home | `!level` |
| buff, rebuff | `!buff` |
| escape, soe | `!soe` |
| giran (or .giran, any of the 11 towns) | `!town giran` |
| town aden, .town aden | `!town aden` |
| teleport to Ruins of Agony, gk Ruins of Agony | `!gk Ruins of Agony` |
| go to Helvetia, walk to Helvetia | `!goto Helvetia` |
| mark Giran square, save place Giran square | `!mark Giran square` |

Anything else is refused with a hint. A typed `!`, `/` or `@` command is checked against the catalog below.

<a id="cmd-town"></a>
### Town teleport (.town)

The leader stops hunting, fights off / steps away, regroups and uses .&lt;town&gt; (the server takes the party along). Giran = the safe regroup trip. A member alone ports itself only when the leader is gone.

- **Sends:** `!town {town}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `town` - Town: town list (Giran, Gludin, Gludio, Dion, Oren, Aden, Hunters, Heine, Goddard, Rune, Schuttgart); default `Giran`
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** teleport giran gludio dion aden oren heine rune goddard schuttgart hunters gludin
- **Example:** `!town Giran`

<a id="cmd-gk"></a>
### Gatekeeper teleport

Walk to the nearest gatekeeper and click the link containing this text. Party: the leader regroups and clicks, the server brings the party; after his teleport + roll call anyone still left behind teleports itself. One member (character target): that character teleports ALONE (its leader may regroup it later).

- **Sends:** `!gk {dest}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `dest` - Destination (link text): gatekeeper destination (type or pick from every live gatekeeper menu); example `Ruins of Agony`
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** teleport gatekeeper port
- **Example:** `!gk Ruins of Agony`

<a id="cmd-goto"></a>
### Walk to…

Walk to an NPC, a saved place (!mark) or "x y". Party target = every member walks. A party leader stops leveling for it and waits at the place for the next order.

- **Sends:** `!goto {place}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `place` - NPC / saved place / x y: free text; example `Helvetia  or  83473 148554`
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** walk move go
- **Example:** `!goto Helvetia or 83473 148554`

<a id="cmd-gotonpc"></a>
### Go to an NPC (anywhere)…

NPC atlas (Scripts/data/npc_atlas.json): the leader takes the party to the best matching NPC — .town to its town, the dungeon way in + room by room (floor teleporters on the way), or teleport near + walk — and opens its dialog. By id (#30487), name (Penelope), role (grocer, gatekeeper, warehouse, priest of dawn, class master, blacksmith … + optional town: "grocer dion") or what it offers ("teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor"). Add a character name at the end for that character alone (any case); a character target that is not the leader = that character alone.

- **Sends:** `!goto npc {npc}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `npc` - NPC / role [town] / teleport:…: free text; example `grocer giran  ·  Penelope  ·  priest of dawn  ·  teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor`
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** npc find walk go priest grocer warehouse gatekeeper atlas
- **Example:** `!goto npc grocer giran · Penelope · priest of dawn · teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor`

- **Search words:** wait giran grocer warehouse

<a id="cmd-soe"></a>

Everyone (leader too) runs out of the fight and uses .townname (never a scroll). Inside a raid / Kamaloka it still retreats (your order wins) but warns in party chat first: raids are normally fought to the end.

- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).

<a id="cmd-formation"></a>
### Formation in town

The party lines up in front of the town landing, side by side (each party its own lane): tank in front, casters, healers at the back. Leveling stops and the members hold their slots until the next order. Scripts/data/formations.json sets the spot.

- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, all parties; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Search words:** line up formation giran landing
- **Example:** `!formation`

<a id="cmd-hunthere"></a>
### Hunt here 24/7

The party hunts around the spot where its leader stands now, around the clock: no supply runs, no Giran regroups, no daily Kamaloka. After a death it comes back here. "!hunthere off" = back to the automatic spots. Not inside a town.

- **Sends:** `!hunthere[ {radius}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `radius` - Radius (800-6000, default 2500): free text; *optional*
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, all parties; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Search words:** hunt here stay 24/7 nonstop farm forever no town
- **Example:** `!hunthere`

Ends Hunt here 24/7 and restores the spot choice from before it (or the automatic spots). A party without Hunt here keeps its choice (answers "was not on").

<a id="cmd-stop"></a>
### STOP everything (switch OFF)

Everyone idle + stop combat, and the party's run switch goes OFF: it does nothing on its own (no leveling, supply runs, regroups, resume after a restart) until Start. Survival, trades and your orders still work. Same as Stop on the party card.

- **Sends:** `!stop`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** halt pause idle off switch
- **Example:** `!stop`

<a id="cmd-start"></a>
### START (switch ON + its activity)

Switches the party ON and starts its configured activity: the raid circuit when it is switched on for the party, else leveling at the chosen spot / hunt here / the leader's pick (Giran regroup first). Already running = nothing new. With a member's name: that member is back with its party (follow + assist). Same as Start on the party card.

- **Sends:** `!start[ {name}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `name` - Only this member (optional): character list (grouped by party); *optional*
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** start run on go resume switch
- **Example:** `!start`

<a id="cmd-ovcast"></a>
### Override: cast a skill

That character casts the skill once (skill id), on: boss | focus | self | &lt;teammate&gt; | &lt;monster in sight&gt; (empty: on its CURRENT target).

- **Sends:** `!ov {name} cast {skill}[ {on}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `name` - Character: character list (grouped by party)
  - `skill` - Skill id: a number; example `1015`
  - `on` - On (boss / focus / self / name): free text; example `boss`; *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy). (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)
- **Where:** search field (command center) · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** override skill cast heal nuke
- **Example:** `!ov Bryndis cast 1015 boss`

That character walks to the dead teammate's body (also mid-raid), targets it and resurrects it: its res skill, a Scroll of Resurrection or a Blessed Scroll (empty: the skill first, else a scroll). The raised one rebuffs first, then follows again.

<a id="cmd-res"></a>
### Resurrect a dead member (best one near)

Every window of the party decides; the best one near acts: a res skill first, else the nearest one with a Scroll of Resurrection (healers and the tank last). Works also when automatic res is off and in a raid (your order). Runs up to 2 min.

- **Sends:** `!res {who}[ {how}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**

  - `how` - How: list; *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).

- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** rez resurrect revive scroll dead raise
- **Example:** `!res Bryndis`

<a id="cmd-ovdrop"></a>

  - `name` - Only this character (empty = everyone who hears it): character list (grouped by party); *optional*

NEVER automatic. Only the named destroyer acts: it goes to Giran (.giran by the normal order rules; a party member is taken there by its leader with the whole party, never alone), walks the recorded routes to the merchants, buys exactly these HP-swap kit pieces (one each; re-checks price + adena before each; never a piece of a slot it already owns; Common copies never), puts NOTHING on (the HP swap wears them only for Frenzy), reports in party chat + Logs/frenzykit_buys.log, then carries on with what it did. <a id="cmd-stash"></a>

Warehouse at Taurin (Giran, recorded route). WHICH warehouse: Scripts/data/stash_rules.json dest (today "clan" = clan members put it into the CLAN warehouse, where only the clan leader can take items out; others the private one) — or pick private / clan for this order. Crafting materials (not the crafter), recipes it cannot use, seal stones, ancient adena, L2Day letters, old gear nobody plans. Consumables, quest items, upgrades stay; untradeable items never go to the clan warehouse. A leader / solo character outside Giran goes there first; members must be in Giran. Fee 30 adena per item. ### Crafter: crystallize items (destroys them)

The crafter turns exactly these pieces of its OWN bag (item object ids, comma separated) into crystals — the items are destroyed. It checks every piece first: never a worn item; enchanted pieces only with the word "enchanted"; special ability / augmented / untradeable / quest items only with "special"; its Crystallize skill level must reach the grade (D 1, C 2, B 3, A 4, S 5). It checks the bag after each one (item gone, crystals up). Build it on the Storage page (Our crafter -&gt; Items -&gt; Turn items into crystals), which shows the crystals you get. Report in party chat + Logs/crystallize.log. Never automatic.

- **Sends:** `!crystallize {name} {ids}[ {flags}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `name` - Which crafter: character list (grouped by party)
  - `ids` - Item object ids (comma separated): free text; example `268481234,268481240`
  - `flags` - Also allow: list; *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that.
- **Where:** search field (command center) · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** crystallize crystals disenchant destroy crafter dwarf gear
- **Example:** `!crystallize Bryndis 268481234,268481240`

<a id="cmd-craftlearn"></a>
### Crafter: learn a recipe from its bag

The crafter uses this recipe (item id) from its bag: it goes into its recipe book and the recipe item is used up. It checks first that its Create Item (or Create Common Item) level is high enough and that the recipe is not already known. A full recipe book (50 on a standard server) refuses it. The Storage page shows a Learn button per recipe.

- **Sends:** `!craft learn {scroll} {name}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `scroll` - Recipe item id: a number; example `1804`
  - `name` - Which crafter: character list (grouped by party)
- **Who acts:** **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy). (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)
- **Where:** search field (command center) · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** craft learn recipe book scroll dwarf
- **Example:** `!craft learn 1804 Bryndis`

<a id="cmd-handover"></a>
### Hand-over (Trade page order)

Run a hand-over the Trade page saved (Logs/handover/&lt;id&gt;.json): each giver goes to the receiver (.townname / walk / route) and trades its list in batches; the receiver stands still and accepts only from our characters. Build orders on the Trade page (#/trade), not here. The same id can be sent again a minute later (after a failed / stopped run); a giver busy with another order says so.

- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).

- **Search words:** trade give hand over clan leader items loot materials
- **Example:** `!handover hm2abc12xyz`

<a id="cmd-enchant"></a>
### Enchant gear (manual only)

NEVER automatic (user). Enchants with the scrolls in the bag. Item empty = every worn piece to the safe +4; or weapon / armor / any words of an item name (worn or in the bag). Level above +4 is allowed: a failed normal scroll destroys the item, a blessed one resets it to +0. Common items and no-grade cannot be enchanted.

- **Sends:** `!enchant {name}[ {item}][ +{to}][ {blessed}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `name` - Character: character list (grouped by party)
  - `item` - Item (empty = all worn; weapon; armor; or part of the name): free text; example `weapon`; *optional*
  - `to` - To level (empty = safe +4): a number; example `4`; *optional*
  - `blessed` - Type blessed to use blessed scrolls: free text; example `blessed`; *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that.
- **Where:** search field (command center) · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** enchant scroll safe blessed weapon armor
- **Example:** `!enchant Bryndis weapon +4 blessed`

- **Search words:** plan jump step

<a id="cat-quest"></a>
## Quests

| Command | Sends | Kind | Safety |
|---|---|---|---|

<a id="cmd-quest"></a>
### Run a quest…

Runs any quest of the datapack (Scripts/data/quests) as a state machine: talk + links, hunt the drops / kills in the best spawn cluster, quest monsters through their trigger, hand-ins. Repeatable quests: repeat N times (forever = until stopped). solo = this character alone (a party member leaves follow; healers cannot hunt solo); party = only the party LEADER acts, the members follow, talk to the same NPCs and report their items (send it to the party / leader). A party target with solo = every member runs it alone. A newer order (!level, !town ...) ends it. State: Logs/quest_state_&lt;Name&gt;.json, page Quests.

- **Sends:** `!quest {quest}[ repeat {repeat}][ {mode}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `quest` - Quest id or name: free text; example `265  ·  Bonds of Slavery`
  - `repeat` - Repeat (repeatable quests): a number or "forever" — empty = once: free text; example `5  ·  forever`; *optional*
  - `mode` - Mode: list; default `solo`
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** one character, several characters, a party; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** quest repeat adena npc hunt turn in hand in
- **Example:** `!quest 265 · Bonds of Slavery repeat 5 · forever solo`

<a id="cmd-queststop"></a>
### Stop the quest

Ends the running quest run after the current step (a party leader also ends the party run). The quest itself stays in the quest log; run it again to continue.

- **Sends:** `!quest stop`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** quest stop
- **Example:** `!quest stop`

- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **safe** - only reports or a dry run; still asks once.
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** quest status
- **Example:** `!quest status`

Quest farm (Scripts/data/quest_farm.json, set on the Quests page -&gt; Quest farm): each farm character says on/off, runs, adena and adena/h, adena traded to the collector. Switching the farm on/off and picking characters happens on the page.

<a id="cmd-scout"></a>
### Scout: is the boss up?

ONE character travels alone to a safe look-out (epics: the guide route, Core = Cruma floors + the Cubic; else teleport near + walk), looks for the boss, writes Logs/raid_status.json (alive / not there; the boss page badge + the raid hunt use it) and Logs/scout_&lt;name&gt;.json, reports in party chat and goes back with .townname — never fights. No name = the leader picks the most expendable free member; never the leader of a busy party.

- **Sends:** `!scout {boss}[ {name}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `boss` - Raid boss (name or id): raid boss (type or pick; list from the Raid bosses tab)
  - `name` - Character (empty = the leader picks one): character list (grouped by party); *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Each character acts for itself**; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
- **Targets:** a party; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Search words:** scout look check up alive epic core orfen queen ant
- **Example:** `!scout Bifrons`

<a id="cmd-whtakeclan"></a>
### Warehouse: take items out (clan)

Only the clan leader can take items out of the clan warehouse on L2Toggle: he walks to the keeper, takes these items (id:count) and, when a character is named, brings them to it with a hand-over (Logs/handover/wht_*.json). A member that gets this order asks the clan leader itself.

- **Sends:** `!whtake {items} clan[ {name}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `items` - Items (id:count, comma separated): free text; example `356:1,1463:500`
  - `name` - For this character (empty = the clan leader keeps it): character list (grouped by party); *optional*
- **Who acts:** Only the **clan leader's** window acts; the target is always the clan leader.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy). (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)
- **Where:** search field (command center) · the clan leader's Commands sheet (character page or his party card)
- **Search words:** clan warehouse withdraw take out gear items
- **Example:** `!whtake 356:1,1463:500 clan`

Report in party chat + Logs/whsell.log. The Storage page sends it with "Take out and sell".

<a id="cmd-clanhand"></a>
### Clan level item to the clan leader now

The character walks / ports to the clan leader and trades him the item the NEXT clan level needs (only as many as he still lacks). Automatic by itself when both are in a town (Clan tab switch "Clan level item hand-over"); this sends it now, wherever he is. Never in a raid / mission / instance / quest / another order of yours.

- **Sends:** `!clanhand`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** one character, several characters, a party; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** blood mark clan level item trade handover leader
- **Example:** `!clanhand`

<a id="cmd-clanskill"></a>

The clan leader learns the focus skill picked on the Clan tab at a village master (here or Gesto / Kusto / Angus in Giran); every clan skill needs clan level 5+.

- **Sends:** `!clanskill`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** Only the **clan leader's** window acts; the target is always the clan leader.
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · the clan leader's Commands sheet (character page or his party card)
- **Example:** `!clanskill`

<a id="cmd-dawn"></a>
### Sign up with the Lords of Dawn

Your order (works whether enrolled on the 7 Signs tab or not): a party = the leader takes the team to the Priest of Dawn in Giran; a character = "!dawn &lt;name&gt;", only that character goes (a party leader takes his party along to Giran, but only he signs up). Always Dawn, never Dusk. No trip during a raid / mission / instance, in the seal validation period or when everyone is signed up already (it says so); a character in a quest is skipped; leveling resumes afterwards. Automatic sign-ups: only parties / characters enrolled on the 7 Signs tab.

- **Sends:** `!dawn`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party, all parties, the clan, one character, several characters; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** seven signs catacomb dawn enroll
- **Example:** `!dawn`

<a id="cmd-b_configset"></a>
### Config: set a value

Live config change (then "Config: save" to keep it). Passwords can never be set here.

- **Sends:** `/config set {key} {value}`
- **Kind:** `/` L2Swarm chat-box command (sent to each chosen character)
- **Arguments:**
  - `key` - Property (as in the XML): free text; example `FollowDistance`
  - `value` - Value: free text
- **Who acts:** each chosen character (L2Swarm does it in that character's window).
- **Targets:** one character, several characters, a party; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that. (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Example:** `/config set FollowDistance Helvetia`

Load a config file from Settings (must be this character's own file: usually named after the LOGIN, e.g. demo60.xml for Demo59; the server checks it). Never tested on 3.8.14.

- **Kind:** `/` L2Swarm chat-box command (sent to each chosen character)

  - `file` - XML in Settings (the account's own file): free text; example `e.g. demo60.xml (login name, not the character)`
- **Who acts:** each chosen character (L2Swarm does it in that character's window).
- **Targets:** one character; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that. (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)

<a id="cmd-p_deploy"></a>
### Deploy swarm.js

Copies Scripts_dev/swarm.js to Scripts/swarm.js after a syntax check (refused within 15 min of the last deploy, during a live raid / Kamaloka, or while accounts log in; "no changes" = nothing done). L2Swarm reloads it on every account (memory per reload); the brain pool reloads it party by party (--watch-script). Never restarts L2Swarm.

- **Sends:** `deploy swarm.js` (label; the dashboard performs it)
- **Kind:** dashboard action (no chat; the dashboard does it itself)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** the dashboard, for the chosen character (here: the PC itself).
- **Targets:** no target (runs on the PC); the form starts with **no target (runs on the PC)**.
- **Safety:** **destructive** - asks once, then you must type `YES`; the server refuses it without that.
- **Where:** search field (command center); also the PC tab
- **Example:** `deploy swarm.js`

<a id="cmd-navtest"></a>

Walk test with logging -&gt; Logs/navtest_&lt;name&gt;.log (disables the bot for 60 s, then switches it back on; the name is case-insensitive).

- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `x` - x: a number
  - `y` - y: a number
  - `name` - Only this character (empty = everyone who hears it): character list (grouped by party); *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** one character, a party; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Example:** `!navtest 83473 148554`

<a id="cmd-escapetest"></a>
### Escape test (no teleport)

Runs the real escape on one character in TEST mode: CC on the nearest monster (only within 900), run to the nearest safe spot, wait for no hits, then STOPS before .townname / Scroll of Escape. Live escape box + map on the Parties tab; result in Logs/escape.log. Refused in raids / Kamaloka / missions and below 70 % HP. No name = the target character (party target = its leader).

- **Sends:** `!escapetest[ {name}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `name` - Character (empty = the one the order goes to): character list (grouped by party); *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** one character, a party; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Search words:** escape flee cc safe spot soe test
- **Example:** `!escapetest`

- **Search words:** escape flee soe test full

<a id="cmd-b_instancezone"></a>
### Instance zone info

Which instances are locked (Kamaloka re-entry times).

- **Sends:** `/instancezone`
- **Kind:** `/` L2Swarm chat-box command (sent to each chosen character)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** each chosen character (L2Swarm does it in that character's window).
- **Targets:** a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with **one character**.
- **Safety:** **safe** - only reports or a dry run; still asks once.
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
- **Example:** `/instancezone`

<a id="cat-legacy"></a>
## Legacy (off in leader mode)

These commands still exist in `swarm.js`, but most of them are switched off in the leader-controlled design (they answer "switched off" or do nothing useful). They are listed so you know what they are; the search puts them last.

| Command | Sends | Kind | Safety |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Farm at the camp point](#cmd-farm) | `!farm` | ! | confirm |
| [Camp here (leader position)](#cmd-camp) | `!camp` | ! | confirm |
| [Set camp point](#cmd-setcamp) | `!setcamp {x} {y} {z}` | ! | confirm |
| [Raid prep (!go)](#cmd-go) | `!go[ {boss}]` | ! | confirm |
| [Raid sequence now (!raid)](#cmd-raidold) | `!raid[ {boss}]` | ! | confirm |
| [Career (solo 1-40)](#cmd-career) | `!career` | ! | confirm |
| [Class-quest escort](#cmd-escort) | `!escort` | ! | confirm |
| [Stop quest (old)](#cmd-queststop_old) | `!queststop` | ! | confirm |
| [Gear share (!gear)](#cmd-gear) | `!gear` | ! | confirm |
| [Shop trip (!shop)](#cmd-shop) | `!shop` | ! | confirm |
| [!kamaloka (placeholder)](#cmd-kamaold) | `!kamaloka` | ! | safe |

<a id="cmd-farm"></a>
### Farm at the camp point

Old farm mode: tank pulls to the camp, others fight in a box (set the camp first).

- **Sends:** `!farm`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Example:** `!farm`

<a id="cmd-camp"></a>
### Camp here (leader position)

The leader broadcasts his position as the camp point.

- **Sends:** `!camp`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:** none
- **Who acts:** The **party leader** acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
- **Targets:** a party; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Example:** `!camp`

<a id="cmd-setcamp"></a>
### Set camp point

Camp point by coordinates.

- **Sends:** `!setcamp {x} {y} {z}`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `x` - x: a number
  - `y` - y: a number
  - `z` - z: a number
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Example:** `!setcamp 83473 148554 -3400`

<a id="cmd-go"></a>
### Raid prep (!go)

Old raid prep: destroyers drain + Frenzy, then the leader posts !raid. Use "Raid a boss" instead.

- **Sends:** `!go[ {boss}]`
- **Kind:** `!` swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
- **Arguments:**
  - `boss` - Boss: raid boss (type or pick; list from the Raid bosses tab); *optional*
- **Who acts:** **Every window that hears it** acts (party target = every member of that party).
- **Targets:** a party; the form starts with **a party**.
- **Safety:** **confirm** - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
- **Where:** search field (command center) · party Commands sheet
- **Example:** `!go`
